This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

08. .  2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Addl. Standing Counsel for the State.
3.
This is an application for grant of bail to appellant.

4. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 376(2)(n)/313 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act in connection with Bangomunda P.S. Case No. 29 of 2015 corresponding to Special G.R. Case No. 11 of 2015 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-,
in default, to further undergo R.I. for a period of one year.
5.
The appeal was filed in the year 2018.
Taking note of the delay in disposal of the appeal, this Court had earlier granted him interim bail.
He has since surrendered to custody in time without misusing the liberty so granted.

It is submitted that the appellant, being the only earning member of the family is required to make necessary arrangements for the sustenance of his family members and since the appeal is unable to be heard finally in the near future, he may be released on bail.
It is further submitted that out of the substantive sentence of 10 years, the appellant has already spent 6 years 9 months in custody.

6. Learned State Counsel has opposed the prayer for bail by submitting that looking at the overwhelming evidence adduced during trial, the appellant was rightly convicted and therefore, no leniency should be shown to him.

sentences.text: 7. Considering the rival submissions and on going through the material on record including the evidence adduced before the trial Court, while not being inclined to grant regular bail, I deem it proper to dispose of the I.A. by directing release of the appellant on interim bail for a period of three months from the date of his actual release on such terms and conditions as the convicting Court may deem fit and proper to impose.
8. I.A. is disposed of.
Sashikanta Mishra) Judge A.K. Rana Designation: PERSONAL ASSISTANT
